findings.description: In one continuous tracking shot the woman walks from a kitchen with light-oak cabinets, tiled backsplash and a countertop microwave, through the hall to the bedroom, then turns and exits back through a doorway into a completely different kitchen: dark cherry cabinets, an over-the-range microwave, a gas range, brown counters and cream walls. Nothing explains the room changing.

The framed blue-flower portrait hung on the hallway wall outside the bedroom (00:01.5-00:04). When she turns to leave the bedroom, the same portrait is on the bedroom's interior wall beside the exit doorway, next to a new green/red painting and a side table with a photo that were never on the hallway side. The geometry of the room around the doorway does not add up.
At 00:00 she wears an open teal V-neck cardigan over a visible white camisole. By 00:03-00:03.25, in front/side view, it is a closed jewel-neck fitted top with no V opening and no camisole.

The picture inside the frame keeps changing. At 00:00 it is a small figure above a blue flower; at 00:01.5-00:02.75 it is a woman's head over a blue flower; at 00:03.25 it reads as a seated dark-haired figure holding a blue object; at 00:07.5 it is a woman's head again. This is generative morphing of the artwork.

During the pan the bedroom reconfigures. At 00:04.5-00:05 there is one window to the right of the bed and a lamp and nightstand on the left. By 00:05.5-00:06 there is also a large curtained window on the left near the headboard. At 00:06.5 a doorway with a paned exterior-style door and a side table appear on that same wall, and the bed/lamp arrangement shifts so it no longer matches the earlier view.

At 00:00 it is a light blonde layered bob with visible fringe. From behind (00:00.75 onward) it reads as a darker brown, pinned-up twist or low updo, then as a loose bob again in profile views. Colour and style drift beyond what the lighting change explains.
